lines.text: Payments fail in a Java application and its threads are left waiting.
A closed circuit breaker lets calls through, but five consecutive failures open it.
While open, it returns an error without calling payments, avoiding the wait.
After two seconds, it becomes half-open and allows a test call.
Success closes it and resumes calls; failure opens it again.
In this simulation, the breaker cut calls during the outage from sixty to twenty-four.
But it still rejected seven requests after payments recovered: protecting resources also means rejecting requests.
